Open annual NIS Parquet files lazily

Source: R/open.R
nis_open.Rd

Open selected years as a DuckDB query.

Usage

nis_open(
  path,
  years = NULL,
  reader = c("duckdb", "arrow"),
  check_release = TRUE
)

Arguments

path

Directory containing NIS_<year>.parquet files or directories.

years

Optional years to open, 2012 or later. Defaults to every matching year with Parquet parts. Explicitly requested years must each have Parquet parts. Years before 2016 are experimental: they hold ICD-9-CM codes in DX*/PR* slots, and 2015 holds both systems (see nis_flag_dx()).

reader

Parquet reader: "duckdb" (default) or "arrow". Arrow is an optional dependency. Its reader preserves source bytes in strings, including malformed UTF-8, and allocates memory outside DuckDB's buffer limit.

check_release

Check annual release totals and design fields by default. Set to FALSE to skip the check.

Value

A lazy DuckDB-backed dbplyr table. Annual source column names are case-normalized. Saved cohorts retain the column names used at export.

Details

Use annual NIS_<year>.parquet files or directories, or Hive directories named YEAR=YYYY. Use one layout per year. The package matches columns by name and checks that recorded years agree with their partitions. The charge fields for 2023 and 2024 remain separate from TOTCHG.

Annual release check

For years with published reference totals, the check compares discharges, the sum of weights, and distinct hospitals when the relevant fields are available. Investigate warnings against the annual release documentation. Invented data and extracts created with nis_write_cohort() are exempt from comparisons with published totals.

Reading into R

Select columns and summarize in DuckDB before calling dplyr::collect(). The default reader rejects malformed UTF-8 when it reads the affected column. Reconvert from a correctly encoded source with nis_convert().

See also

Prepare annual NIS files.

Other data-access: nis_convert(), nis_example(), nis_label()

Examples

path <- nis_example(years = 2019:2020)
#> duckdb keeps downloaded extensions and secrets in a temporary directory:
#> ℹ /tmp/RtmpUnGnxo/duckdb
#> This is removed when the R session ends.
#> • Extensions are re-downloaded each session.
#> • Secrets are lost.
#> ℹ Run duckdb(shared_home = TRUE) (or create ~/.duckdb) to keep them (suitable for most users).
#> ℹ Run duckdb(shared_home = FALSE) to accept the temporary directory (and silence this message).
#> ℹ See ?duckdb_storage for details and alternatives.
nis <- nis_open(path)
#> duckdb keeps downloaded extensions and secrets in a temporary directory:
#> ℹ /tmp/RtmpUnGnxo/duckdb
#> This is removed when the R session ends.
#> • Extensions are re-downloaded each session.
#> • Secrets are lost.
#> ℹ Run duckdb(shared_home = TRUE) (or create ~/.duckdb) to keep them (suitable for most users).
#> ℹ Run duckdb(shared_home = FALSE) to accept the temporary directory (and silence this message).
#> ℹ See ?duckdb_storage for details and alternatives.
nis |>
  dplyr::count(YEAR) |>
  dplyr::collect()
#> # A tibble: 2 × 2
#>    YEAR     n
#>   <int> <dbl>
#> 1  2020    96
#> 2  2019    96

# Open one year only
nis_open(path, years = 2020) |>
  dplyr::count(YEAR) |>
  dplyr::collect()
#> duckdb keeps downloaded extensions and secrets in a temporary directory:
#> ℹ /tmp/RtmpUnGnxo/duckdb
#> This is removed when the R session ends.
#> • Extensions are re-downloaded each session.
#> • Secrets are lost.
#> ℹ Run duckdb(shared_home = TRUE) (or create ~/.duckdb) to keep them (suitable for most users).
#> ℹ Run duckdb(shared_home = FALSE) to accept the temporary directory (and silence this message).
#> ℹ See ?duckdb_storage for details and alternatives.
#> # A tibble: 1 × 2
#>    YEAR     n
#>   <int> <dbl>
#> 1  2020    96
